worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the $x$ terms and complete the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}+54y-27 & =0 \\ 9({y}^{2}+6y)-4{x}^{2}-27 & =0 \\ 9\,[(y+3)^{2}-9]-4{x}^{2}-27 & =0 \\ 9(y+3)^{2}-81-4{x}^{2}-27 & =0 \\ 9(y+3)^{2}-4{x}^{2} & =108 \\ \frac{9(y+3)^{2}}{108}-\frac{4{x}^{2}}{108} & =1 \\ \frac{(y+3)^{2}}{12}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{27} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The asymptotes of a vertical hyperbola

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{a}{b}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k)=(0,-3),\,a=\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt{3},\,b=\sqrt{27}=3\sqrt{3}.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(-3) & =\pm (\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3\sqrt{3}})(x-0) \\ y+3 & =\pm \,\frac{2}{3}x.\end{aligned}
$$
